INTRODUCTION
The South Carolina chapter of Trout Unlimited would like to thank the Federal Power Commission for the opportunity to offer comments to the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project Draft Environmental Impact Statement. Sportsmen organizations such as T.U. have in the recent past become painfully aware of the major reductions in cold water habitats in the project area. The value of the Howard Creek drainage is much greater to the citizens of South Carolina than the few miles of stream would indicate. This is due to the almost total loss of cold water streams in the "Keowee River" basin. The intensive timber harvesting and associated road construction in the remaining lands in this basin have degraded a large portion of the remaining waters from their past high quality state. The cold water resource situation has reached in the past ten years a critical state. Each additional loss of habitat not only depletes the resource but shifts existing pressures to the remaining resource with a resulting degradation.
The premier second story trout fishery which has been developed in Lake Jocassee and the resulting spawning run into tributary streams has gone a long way to replace the lost stream habitats. The fate of this entire fishery is now in question due to numerous factors associated with power production at Keowee, Jocassee, Bad Creek and proposed projects on other tributary. The value of these habitats has not been realistically addressed by the Applicant.
These are the concerns which we have for our unique resource. We are committed to the preservation of our shrinking habitats and the enhancement of the remaining resource which has been degraded. Our commitment to watershed and resource conservation forces us to oppose the continuing and systematic loss of habitat and insist that the substantial questions raised by this project be addressed.
No comment required.
These issues have been discussed in Sections 2.2.2.2, 3.1.2.3, 3.2.2.3, and 9.2.
No comment required.
